title: Palestinian History: The People of Filastin

connections.label: Persian, Greek, Roman and Byzantine rule

events.label: Natufian culture
events.blurb: Natufian foragers in Palestine build some of the earliest permanent villages in the world, a deep local past that Palestinian historians emphasize.

events.label: Jericho (Tell es-Sultan)
events.blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited towns, with a stone tower from about 8000 BCE; UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage site in the State of Palestine in 2023.

events.label: Ghassulian culture
events.blurb: Chalcolithic villagers near Jericho and Beersheba farm, herd and work copper (dates approximate).

events.label: Canaanite towns arise
events.blurb: Walled towns develop across Canaan in the Early Bronze Age, the beginning of the city-state world.

events.label: Amarna letters
events.blurb: Canaanite kings of Urusalim (Jerusalem), Gezer and Shechem write to the Egyptian pharaoh (c. 1350 BCE).

events.label: Philistines settle the coast
events.blurb: Aegean-origin Sea Peoples settle Gaza, Ashkelon and Ashdod and mix with Canaanites; their name later becomes Palestine.

events.label: Israel and Judah in the hills
events.blurb: Highland kingdoms emerge from the local Canaanite population; Ben-Gurion and Ben-Zvi themselves argued in 1918 that the fellahin descended largely from these ancient Jewish farmers.

events.label: Assyrian conquests
events.blurb: Assyria conquers Samaria and the Philistine cities and settles deportees from elsewhere in its empire.

events.label: Babylon destroys Ashkelon
events.blurb: Nebuchadnezzar sacks Philistine Ashkelon, and later Jerusalem in 586 BCE.

events.label: Herodotus names Palaistine
events.blurb: The Greek historian calls the coastal region Palaistine Syria, the earliest known use of the name in Greek.

events.label: Alexander besieges Gaza
events.blurb: Gaza resists Alexander for two months; Greek cities and culture spread through the land.

events.label: Roman rule begins
events.blurb: Pompey brings the region under Rome.

events.label: Province renamed Syria Palaestina
events.blurb: After crushing the Bar Kokhba revolt Hadrian renames Judea; the name Palestine continues through Byzantine, Arab and Ottoman rule.

events.label: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
events.blurb: Constantine's churches in Jerusalem and Bethlehem anchor the Palestinian Christian community, one of the oldest in the world.

events.label: Palaestina Prima, Secunda, Tertia
events.blurb: Byzantine administration divides the land into three provinces named Palestine (c. 400 CE).

events.label: Sasanian conquest
events.blurb: Persian forces take Jerusalem before Byzantium recovers it in 629.

events.label: Arab conquest; Umar in Jerusalem
events.blurb: Caliph Umar receives Jerusalem's surrender (637 or 638); Arabic and Islam spread among the local population gradually over centuries.

events.label: Jund Filastin
events.blurb: The Arab district of Filastin, later governed from Ramla, keeps the Roman name in Arabic.

events.label: Dome of the Rock
events.blurb: Caliph Abd al-Malik completes the Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif (691/692).

events.label: Al-Aqsa Mosque built
events.blurb: The Umayyads build al-Aqsa, the third holiest mosque in Islam (dates approximate).

events.label: Ramla founded
events.blurb: The only town founded by the Arabs in Palestine becomes the capital of Jund Filastin.

events.label: Crusaders take Jerusalem
events.blurb: Crusaders massacre Muslim and Jewish inhabitants and found the Latin Kingdom.

events.label: Salah al-Din retakes Jerusalem
events.blurb: After victory at Hattin, Salah al-Din restores Muslim rule over al-Quds.

events.label: Battle of Ain Jalut
events.blurb: The Mamluks halt the Mongol advance near Jenin.

events.label: Nabi Musa shrine
events.blurb: Sultan Baybars builds the shrine near Jericho whose yearly festival later becomes a Palestinian national gathering.

events.label: Ottoman conquest
events.blurb: Selim I takes Palestine, beginning four centuries of Ottoman rule.

events.label: Suleiman rebuilds Jerusalem's walls
events.blurb: The walls of the Old City standing today are built.

events.label: Zahir al-Umar's Galilee
events.blurb: An Arab sheikh rules much of northern Palestine from Acre, cited by Palestinian historians as an early local polity (dates approximate).

events.label: Napoleon fails at Acre
events.blurb: Acre's defenders turn back the French army.

events.label: Peasants' revolt of 1834
events.blurb: Fellahin and notables rise against Egyptian conscription under Ibrahim Pasha; some historians treat it as a formative moment for Palestinian identity.

events.label: Ottoman Land Code
events.blurb: Land registration lets absentee owners take title to land farmed by villagers, land later sold to Zionist buyers.

events.label: First land clash with settlers
events.blurb: Villagers who lost land near Petah Tikva clash with Zionist settlers, an early recorded dispute.

events.label: Filastin newspaper founded
events.blurb: Issa and Yousef al-Issa's Jaffa paper addresses its readers as Palestinians and warns against Zionist colonization.

events.label: Hussein-McMahon correspondence
events.blurb: Britain promises Arab independence in exchange for revolt against the Ottomans; Arabs understood Palestine to be included, which Britain later denied.

events.label: Wa'd Balfour (Balfour Declaration)
events.blurb: Britain promises a Jewish national home in a land about 90 percent Arab, referring to them only as 'non-Jewish communities'; Palestinians mark it each November.

events.label: Palestine Arab Congresses
events.blurb: Notables organize congresses to oppose the Mandate and Zionist immigration.

events.label: Nabi Musa uprising
events.blurb: The Nabi Musa festival in Jerusalem turns into the first major riots against British and Zionist plans.

events.label: British Mandate imposed
events.blurb: The League of Nations gives Britain a mandate that writes the Balfour Declaration into law.

events.label: Buraq Revolt
events.blurb: Clashes over the Western Wall (al-Buraq) spread, including killings of Jews in Hebron and Safed; Britain hangs Fuad Hijazi, Muhammad Jamjoum and Ata al-Zir in 1930.

events.label: Izz al-Din al-Qassam killed
events.blurb: The preacher who led armed resistance in the north is killed by British police, becoming a lasting symbol.

events.label: The Great Revolt
events.blurb: A six-month general strike and armed uprising against British rule and Zionist immigration; Britain crushes it and roughly 5,000 Arabs are killed (estimates vary).

events.label: UN Partition Resolution 181
events.blurb: The UN proposes about 55 percent of the land for a Jewish state when Jews were about a third of the population and owned under 7 percent of the land.

events.label: Deir Yassin massacre
events.blurb: Irgun and Lehi fighters kill over 100 villagers near Jerusalem, and news of the killings drives flight elsewhere.

events.label: Al-Nakba
events.blurb: About 750,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled, more than 400 villages are depopulated, and Israel bars their return.

events.label: UN Resolution 194
events.blurb: The General Assembly resolves that refugees wishing to return home should be permitted to do so.

events.label: UNRWA established
events.blurb: The UN agency for Palestine refugees begins serving camps in Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon.

events.label: Military rule inside Israel
events.blurb: Palestinians who remained and became Israeli citizens live under military government with travel permits until 1966.

events.label: Kafr Qasim massacre
events.blurb: Israeli border police kill 49 Palestinian citizens returning from their fields after an unannounced curfew.

events.label: Fatah founded
events.blurb: Yasser Arafat and others found a movement for Palestinian-led armed struggle.

events.label: PLO founded
events.blurb: The Palestine Liberation Organization forms in Jerusalem; Fatah takes over its leadership in 1969.

events.label: Al-Naksa
events.blurb: Israel occupies the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza; about 300,000 Palestinians are displaced, many for a second time.

events.label: Battle of Karameh
events.blurb: Fedayeen and Jordanian forces resist an Israeli raid, boosting the guerrilla movement.

events.label: Black September
events.blurb: The Jordanian army drives the PLO out of Jordan, killing thousands.

events.label: Land Day
events.blurb: Israeli forces kill six Palestinian citizens protesting land confiscation in the Galilee; it is commemorated every March 30.

events.label: Sabra and Shatila massacre
events.blurb: Lebanese Phalangists, in an area controlled by the Israeli army, kill hundreds to over 2,000 refugees (estimates vary); an Israeli inquiry found Sharon bore personal responsibility.

events.label: First Intifada
events.blurb: A mass civil uprising of strikes, boycotts and stone-throwing against occupation; about 1,100 Palestinians are killed.

events.label: Declaration of Independence
events.blurb: The PNC in Algiers proclaims the State of Palestine in a text drafted by poet Mahmoud Darwish, implicitly accepting the 1967 lines.

events.label: Oslo Accords
events.blurb: The PLO recognizes Israel, which recognizes the PLO but not a Palestinian state; critics such as Edward Said called it a surrender.

events.label: Palestinian Authority formed
events.blurb: Arafat returns and limited self-rule begins in Gaza and Jericho.

events.label: Ibrahimi Mosque massacre
events.blurb: Settler Baruch Goldstein kills 29 Muslim worshippers in Hebron.

events.label: Camp David summit fails
events.blurb: Talks collapse over borders, Jerusalem and refugees.

events.label: Al-Aqsa Intifada
events.blurb: Sharon's visit to the Haram al-Sharif is followed by a second, armed uprising; roughly 3,000 Palestinians are killed by 2005.

events.label: The Wall
events.blurb: Israel builds a barrier largely inside the West Bank; the ICJ advised in 2004 that the route violates international law.

events.label: Death of Yasser Arafat
events.blurb: Arafat dies in Paris after years besieged in his Ramallah compound.

events.label: Hamas wins elections
events.blurb: Hamas wins the legislative elections; in 2007 Fatah and Hamas split between the West Bank and Gaza.

events.label: Siege of Gaza
events.blurb: Israel and Egypt impose a land, sea and air blockade on Gaza's two million people.

events.label: Gaza war 2008-09
events.blurb: About 1,400 Palestinians are killed in Israel's Operation Cast Lead.

events.label: UN non-member observer state
events.blurb: The General Assembly upgrades Palestine's status by a large majority.

events.label: Gaza war 2014
events.blurb: About 2,250 Palestinians are killed, most of them civilians, in 51 days.

events.label: Ancient DNA study of Canaanites
events.blurb: Agranat-Tamir et al. in Cell find that modern Levantine populations carry substantial Bronze Age Southern Levant ancestry.

events.label: Great March of Return
events.blurb: Weekly protests at the Gaza fence demand return; Israeli snipers kill over 200.

events.label: Sheikh Jarrah and the Unity Intifada
events.blurb: Evictions in Jerusalem spark protests by Palestinians in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza.

events.label: October 7 attack
events.blurb: Hamas-led fighters break out of besieged Gaza, kill about 1,200 people in Israel, most of them civilians, and seize 251 hostages; Hamas named it the Al-Aqsa Flood.

events.label: Genocide war on Gaza
events.blurb: Over 73,000 Palestinians killed by late 2026 according to the Gaza Health Ministry, most of the Strip destroyed and its people repeatedly displaced; Palestinians call it harb al-ibada, the war of extermination.

events.label: ICJ orders provisional measures
events.blurb: In South Africa's genocide case the court orders Israel to prevent genocidal acts and allow aid.

events.label: ICJ: occupation is unlawful
events.blurb: An advisory opinion finds Israel's continued occupation unlawful and calls for its end as rapidly as possible.

events.label: Famine confirmed in Gaza City
events.blurb: The IPC famine review confirms famine in Gaza governorate.

events.label: UN Commission finds genocide
events.blurb: The UN Commission of Inquiry chaired by Navi Pillay concludes that Israel committed genocide in Gaza; Israel rejects the finding.

events.label: UK, France, Canada, Australia recognize Palestine
events.blurb: Major Western states recognize the State of Palestine at the UN General Assembly.

events.label: Ceasefire and prisoner release
events.blurb: Israel releases nearly 2,000 prisoners in exchange for the hostages, but strikes continue and over 1,000 more Palestinians are killed by 2026 per the Health Ministry.

events.label: Record displacement in the West Bank
events.blurb: At least 37,000 Palestinians are displaced in 2025 by raids and settler attacks, a record, and B'Tselem reports 21 communities uprooted.
